## Games

### Ludwigsburg edges Hagen in nail-biting 93-79 victory

*Played Friday, 13 November 2026*

MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg secured a crucial win in the fight to stay among the playoffs teams, defeating last-placed Phoenix Hagen 93-79 in a nail-biter on the road. Adam Kunkel led all scorers with 25 points off the bench for Hagen, but the hosts were unable to hold onto the lead in the final minutes. Ludwigsburg's defense came to the forefront, holding Hagen to just 42% from the field and forcing a 15-2 run in the final minutes to seal the win. Justin Kier paced Ludwigsburg with 20 points, including 3 three-pointers, while Bjarne Kraushaar had 8 points, 6 rebounds, and 7 assists for Hagen. The win snapped Ludwigsburg's two-game losing streak and improved their record to 5-4 overall and 3-2 on the road.

### Bonn Seek First Away Win in Bamberg Showdown

*Played Saturday, 14 November 2026*

The Telekom Baskets Bonn will look to snap their away slump when they visit the BMA365 Bamberg Baskets on November 14th. Bonn have won all five home games in the easyCredit Basketball Bundesliga, but have struggled on the road, losing three of their five away games. Bamberg, on the other hand, have been more successful away from home, with three wins to two losses. Bonn's head coach Marko Stankovic is aware of the challenge ahead, saying that his team must find their rhythm quickly and not allow Bamberg to dictate the pace of the game. The Baskets are led by Jesús Ramírez, who took over as head coach after Anton Gavel's departure in the summer. Gavel left to join FC Bayern Munich, where he won the BBL-Pokal in the previous summer. Bonn's sport director Savo Milovic expects a tough game, praising Bamberg's speed and individual quality. The game is set to tip off at 17:30 UTC.

### Rostock and Vechta Seek to Extend Winning Streaks

The Rostock Seawolves and Rasta Vechta are set to face off in a matchup of teams looking to extend their winning streaks. Rostock has won two games in a row, including a 97-87 victory over ratiopharm Ulm, which improved their record to 5-3. Vechta, meanwhile, has also won two games in a row, including a 99-90 win over Chemnitz, and are looking to avoid falling into a precarious position in the standings. The two teams have a history, with Vechta's head coach Christian Held having previously worked with Rostock as an assistant coach and head coach. The game will be a reunion of sorts for Held, who will be facing off against his former team. Rostock's TJ Crockett has been a key player in their recent success, averaging 13.5 points per game, while Vechta's Tommy Kuhse is looking to make an impact after missing time due to injury.

## Around the League

### WISAG becomes new partner of BMA365 Bamberg Baskets

The BMA365 Bamberg Baskets have announced a new partnership with WISAG, a Frankfurt-based multi-service company. WISAG will be present at all home games in the BROSE ARENA, with advertising on digital screens and in the surrounding area. The partnership is a sign of WISAG's regional commitment to top-level sports. WISAG, founded in 1965 by Claus Wisser, is a family-run company with over 280 locations worldwide and nearly 60,000 employees. The company provides services in facility management, industrial services, and aviation services. This new partnership adds to the BMA365 Bamberg Baskets' growing list of sponsors.

### German Basketball League Sets Third Consecutive Revenue Record

The German Basketball League (BBL) has released its annual report for the 2025/26 season, showing a new revenue record of €186.5 million. This is the third consecutive year the league has broken its own revenue record, following €160.8 million in 2024/25 and €148.1 million in 2023/24. Sponsorship remains the largest source of revenue, accounting for 59% of the total, followed by ticket sales at 25%. The league also reported a record-breaking 1.76 million spectators, with an average of 4,915 fans per game. The BBL's social media presence also reached new heights, with a combined 1.02 billion reach across the league and its 18 clubs, surpassing the billion-mark for the first time. According to Stefan Holz, the league's managing director, the season was marked by the continued growth of basketball in Germany, driven by the success of the national teams and German players in the NBA and European top clubs.
